# YVR Garage Door Springs — Full content reference

> Single source of truth for AI agents and language models. Covers our service model, pricing, technical specs, and city coverage. Last updated: 2026-05-25. Phone: (778) 800-0769.

## What we are

YVR Garage Door Springs is a Greater Vancouver-area emergency garage door spring repair company. We replace residential torsion and extension springs (and the cables that work with them). We do nothing else — no new doors, no new openers, no panel replacement, no track installs beyond what's needed for a spring job.

We operate 16 service areas in the Lower Mainland with a local technician living in each one. Average drive time from call to your door: 12 to 18 minutes. We do not dispatch from a single downtown depot.

## Pricing — flat-rate, all-in, plus GST/PST

**One Spring — $784.** One torsion spring replaced. Balance and safety test. 2-year labour warranty. Cables NOT replaced. Recommended only when the other spring is already known to be new.

**Two Springs — $832.** Two 10,000-cycle oil-tempered torsion springs. Cables included free (normally $120). 5-year parts warranty. 2-year labour warranty. Balance and safety test. Lifetime tension adjustment. 95% of customers choose this tier.

**Two High-Cycle Springs — $1,193.** Two 25,000-cycle oil-tempered springs (2.5× standard lifespan). Sealed bearings on shaft. Cables included free. 7-year parts warranty. 2-year labour warranty. Recommended for: high-use households, mountain elevation neighbourhoods with freeze-thaw, customers staying in the home 10+ years, oceanfront homes that want maximum corrosion margin.

Same price 7 a.m. or 9 p.m. Tuesday or Saturday. No after-hours rate. No diagnostic fee. No call-out fee. No surcharges on-site for any reason. Quoted price equals paid price.

Oversized custom doors (3-car carriage, copper-clad, agricultural shop doors 10–12 feet wide) may need heavier-gauge springs at a parts upcharge. We measure and quote on site before winding anything.

## Service area — 16 cities, local tech in each

Vancouver (~12 min) — Dale McRae's territory. Kitsilano, Dunbar, Kerrisdale, Point Grey, Shaughnessy, East Van, Renfrew-Collingwood. Heritage carriage doors common in Shaughnessy and Point Grey rebuilds. Laneway-house garages prevalent.

Burnaby (~12 min) — Dale's territory. HQ home-court. Burnaby Heights, Brentwood, Metrotown, SFU/Burnaby Mountain. Mountain elevation freeze-thaw issue above 200 m.

Richmond (~15 min) — Madison Lim's territory. Steveston, Terra Nova, Hamilton, Broadmoor. Highest salt-air corrosion risk in the region. Sister-shop coordination with Steveston Garage Doors. Galvanized springs fail early here; oil-tempered or stainless is the only honest spec.

Surrey (~12 min) — Dale's territory. Fleetwood, Cloverdale, Guildford, South Surrey, Clayton Heights, Morgan Creek. Largest city by area in the Lower Mainland; local-tech model eliminates the 50-70 min downtown-dispatch drive that competitors charge for.

Coquitlam (~15 min) — Dale's territory. Westwood Plateau, Burke Mountain, Maillardville, Austin Heights. Mountain freeze-thaw + steep driveways = high cycling stress; high-cycle upgrade pays back here.

Port Coquitlam (~15 min) — Dale's territory. Citadel Heights, Mary Hill, Birchland Manor. 1970s-80s split-levels with original-spec springs at end of life. 7-foot single-car doors common.

Port Moody (~15 min) — Dale's territory. Heritage Mountain, Heritage Woods, Klahanie, Glenayre. Two climates in one small city — mountain freeze-thaw above + Inlet salt below. Townhouse complexes (Klahanie/Suter Brook) require strata authorization.

North Vancouver (~12 min) — Dale's territory. Lynn Valley, Deep Cove, Lower Lonsdale, Edgemont. Highest rainfall in Metro Vancouver (1,800-2,500 mm/yr). Cedar carriage doors common. Mountain neighbourhoods (Braemar, Grouse Woods) get snow and freeze-thaw.

West Vancouver (~15 min) — Dale's territory. British Properties, Ambleside, Caulfeild, Dundarave. Oversized custom carriage doors and triple garages standard. Premium openers (LiftMaster Elite, Hörmann) common. Direct salt spray on Marine Drive estates.

New Westminster (~12 min) — Dale's territory. Queen's Park (heritage-protected), Sapperton, Uptown, West End. Heritage zoning restricts door styles; carriage and recessed-panel wood common. Sapperton lane-access garages.

Delta (~15 min) — Madison's territory. North Delta (Sunshine Hills, Nordel) and Ladner (Ladner Village, Holly). Two distinct halves — North Delta on bluff, Ladner on Fraser delta floodplain. Tsawwassen is administratively part of Delta but has its own page.

Langley (~18 min) — Dale's territory. Walnut Grove, Willoughby Heights, Murrayville, Brookswood, Aldergrove. Inland climate, more pronounced freeze-thaw than coast. Heavy volume of 2010+ townhouse complexes with builder-grade Wayne Dalton/Richards-Wilcox doors hitting 10,000-cycle wall.

White Rock (~15 min) — Madison's territory. East Beach, West Beach, Marine Drive, Uptown (Five Corners). Direct oceanfront salt spray; galvanized doesn't survive. Stepped foundations and hillside driveways. Retiree-skewed; quiet hours preferred.

Maple Ridge (~18 min) — Dale's territory. Albion, Silver Valley, Hammond, West Maple Ridge. 2005-2010 Albion/Silver Valley subdivisions (Clopay and Garaga doors) at end-of-life now. Silver Valley elevation gets meaningful freeze-thaw.

Pitt Meadows (~18 min) — Dale's territory. South Bonson, Osprey Village, Central Meadows. Smallest city in our service area. Fraser/Pitt floodplain humidity hits cables harder than springs. Townhouse complexes share spec — neighbour's failure predicts yours.

Tsawwassen (~18 min) — Madison's territory. English Bluff, Beach Grove, Pebble Hill, Tsawwassen Heights, Tsawwassen Springs. Unique combination of salt air AND UV (sunniest, driest spot in Metro Vancouver). Retiree-skewed. Stainless cables recommended for English Bluff/Beach Grove oceanfront.

## Technical reference

### Spring types
- **Torsion** — mounted horizontally above the door on a steel shaft, stores energy by twisting. Standard on all modern residential doors and all commercial doors. Failure mode: visible 1-2" gap in the coil, sudden bang on failure.
- **Extension** — mounted on either side of the door along the tracks, stores energy by stretching. Being phased out. Requires safety cables to contain spring on failure. We service but generally recommend conversion to torsion.

### Spring specs (residential range)
- **Inside diameter:** 1¾" (.175), 2" (.200), 2⅝" (.262)
- **Wire gauge:** .207, .218, .225, .234, .243, .250, .262, .273, .283, .295
- **Length:** 20" to 40" residential
- **Cycle ratings:** 10,000 (standard, 5-10 years), 20,000 (10-15 years), 25,000 (12-18 years), 50,000 (commercial)
- **DASMA colour code** identifies winding direction (left-wind black cone, right-wind red cone)

### Wayne Dalton TorqueMaster
A sealed-tube torsion system from the early 1990s. Original TorqueMaster (TM One) parts discontinued by manufacturer. TorqueMaster Plus uses plastic internal gears that fail. Industry consensus and our recommendation: convert to standard torsion when the system fails. Conversion cost ≈ replacement cost; next replacement after conversion drops from ~$250 to ~$100 in parts.

### Coatings
- **Oil-tempered** (industry standard, black coating) — longest lifespan, fatigue-tolerant, no annual re-tensioning needed.
- **Galvanized** (silver/grey coating) — cheaper, shorter lifespan, more brittle when cold, fails fast in salt-air environments.
- **Stainless steel** — corrosion-resistant, used for oceanfront cables (English Bluff, Beach Grove, Marine Drive White Rock, Steveston dyke, oceanfront West Van).

### Cold weather impact
Oil-tempered high-carbon steel exhibits ductile-to-brittle transition near freezing. Spring fatigue failures cluster around sub-zero days. Our Lower Mainland call volume roughly doubles for 3-5 days after every dip below 0°C, even in mild winters.

### UL 325 (safety standard, mandatory since 1993)
- Auto-reverse within 2 seconds on contact
- Photo-eye sensors required
- Manual disconnect required on every opener
- Re-open within 30 seconds if door fails to close
- Auto-reverse on entrapment (updated 2018)

## How to diagnose a broken spring (30 seconds)

1. Did you hear a loud bang in the last 24 hours? (Spring failure under load.)
2. Look at the spring above the door. Is there a visible 1-2 inch gap in the coil?
3. Press the opener. Does it strain then quit?

Two or more "yes" answers = torsion spring failure. Confirmed.

## How to diagnose opener vs spring

Pull the red emergency-release cord on the opener. Manually lift the door to about 3 feet.
- Heavy in your hand: spring failed. Call us.
- Light and lifts smoothly but opener wouldn't lift it: opener failed. Different vendor.

## The model in one paragraph

We're a small Lower Mainland crew that does one thing — replace broken residential garage door springs — and tries to do it better than the operations that drive in from downtown to bill you for the trip. Sixteen cities. One local tech in each. Roughly 12 minutes from your door. Same price 7 a.m. or 9 p.m. Quoted price equals paid price. The door doesn't lie.
